episode.subject: juvenile American alligator and turtle on log
episode.title: A practice attempt
episode.body:
I told him I could stay out of the water longer than he could.

He tucked his feet into his shell.

I tucked mine against my sides and slid off the log.

When I climbed back, he had put his feet out again.

I rested my chin on his shell and told him I hadn't started yet.

proposals.visibleScene: Banded juvenile American alligator rests its chin across a larger turtle shell on a narrow partially submerged log. Alligator front feet grip log, rear feet and long tail visible; turtle head and feet extend. Both animals are dry above water except alligator tail end.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Friendly contest, tucked feet, slip into water, climbing back and attempted restart are fictional. Photo establishes returned log posture, not a recorded fall or behavioral experiment. Alligator merely folds feet against sides, never retracts limbs into shell. Turtle species and sex not established; unnamed male is fictional casting. Neither turtle nor gator provides protection, rescues another, or responds to pressure with speech-triggered chin movement.
proposals.continuity: Young Mabel memory after I was going to hide and before adult avatar stage. Preserve original two Stories word for word, female identity, Everglades home and avatar. New Orleans Louisiana is source provenance within American alligator range, not a narrated journey. Relative size, striped tail and juvenile shape support childhood; precise age not claimed.
proposals.biologyEvidence: Full NPS Everglades species account independently opened: Alligator mississippiensis freshwater distribution in southeastern United States, juvenile crossbands fading with age. Does not document this contest or infer photographed sex.
proposals.authorReview: Unlike held high-part draft, this is imitation of a different body, physical consequence and attempted renegotiation of a losing contest. Own feet fold normally, no invented anatomy. Image has visible grain; root already opened and found contact legible. New prose still pending independent decision. Possible remaining concern: juvenile competitive embarrassment is familiar elsewhere, though absent in Mabel current arc. Root reviewed the revised draft as distinct and physically plausible fiction; final independent package review remains pending. Title changed to A practice attempt at lead suggestion to avoid repeating body wording.

heldDrafts.title: The high part
heldDrafts.body:
I put my chin down on the highest part of the log.

The highest part told me to move it.

I lifted my chin. A head came out at the far end and looked back at me.

I said I hadn't known.

He said he'd noticed.

I lay down beside him. This time I kept my head on my own feet.
heldDrafts.reason: Root identified exact repeated mechanism from I called first: chin rests on somebody, that body speaks, Mabel lifts chin. Preserve draft; never admit this version.

Apparently forgot to post this one. We were under the lot tree watching for warblers and someone else came by and went down to the dock to fish. The gator immediately surfaced behind our neighbor's house and made a beeline for the dock which it stopped maybe about 12 to 15 feet away from. 

Eventually it moved on and passed under the bridge. Pretty interesting encounter. There's 3 gators we know of in the lake and this is the medium sized animal. Somewhere between 4 and 5 feet would be my best guess.
